title: To Be · Questions
context: Are you a student? Yes, I am.
Is she a doctor at the hospital? Yes, she is.
Where is the library?
Who is that? That is my brother.
What is your job? I am a driver.
Why are you late?
How are you? I am fine, thank you.
grammar: To ask a question using be, move am/is/are before the subject: Are you a student? Is she a doctor? Use short answers matching the verb: Yes, I am; No, I'm not; Yes, she is. Add Who, What, Where, Why or How for information questions.
grammarExamples: Are you a student? Yes, I am.
Is she a doctor? Yes, she is.
Where is the library?
express: Você é um estudante? - Sim, eu sou. / Não, não sou.
Are you a student? Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
Ela é médica no hospital? - Sim, ela é.
Is she a doctor at the hospital? Yes, she is.
Onde fica a biblioteca?
Where is the library?
Quem é aquele? - Aquele é meu irmão.
Who is that? That is my brother.
Qual é o seu trabalho? - Eu sou motorista.
What is your job? I am a driver.
Por que você está atrasado?
Why are you late?
Como você está? - Estou bem, obrigado.
How are you? I am fine, thank you.
gaps: Is he a pilot? Yes, he ___.

title: Present Simple · Don't / Doesn't
context: I like coffee, but I don't like tea.
She works in an office, but she doesn't work on Saturdays.
He plays soccer, but he doesn't play basketball.
We watch TV in the evening, but we never watch the news.
It rains in winter, but it doesn't rain every day.
You speak English, but you don't speak Spanish.
grammar: Use don't + base verb with I, you, we and they: I don't drink tea. Use doesn't + base verb with he, she and it: She doesn't work on Saturdays. After doesn't, don't add -s to the main verb. Frequency words (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) describe habits, and but contrasts two facts.
grammarExamples: I don't like tea.
She doesn't work on Saturdays.
He plays soccer, but he doesn't play basketball.
express: Eu gosto de café, mas não gosto de chá.
I like coffee, but I don't like tea.
Ela trabalha em um escritório, mas não trabalha aos sábados.
She works in an office, but she doesn't work on Saturdays.
Ele joga futebol, mas não joga basquete.
He plays soccer, but he doesn't play basketball.
Nós assistimos TV à noite, mas nunca assistimos ao jornal.
We watch TV at night, but we never watch the news.
Chove no inverno, mas não chove todos os dias.
It rains in winter, but it doesn't rain every day.
Eles leem livros, mas não leem jornais.
They read books, but they don't read newspapers.
Você fala inglês, mas não fala espanhol.
You speak English, but you don't speak Spanish.

title: Present Simple · Do / Does Questions
context: Do you live in the city? Yes, I do.
Does she speak Portuguese? Yes, she does.
What do you study? I study English.
Where does he work? He works in a school.
When do they watch movies? They watch movies on weekends.
chunks: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.
grammar: Use Do + I/you/we/they + base verb for Present Simple questions. Use Does + he/she/it + base verb. The main verb never takes -s after does: Does she speak? NOT Does she speaks? Respond with Yes, I do / No, I don't; Yes, she does / No, she doesn't. For information questions, begin with what, where, when or why.
grammarExamples: Do you live in the city? Yes, I do.
Does she speak Portuguese? Yes, she does.
What do you study? I study English.
express: Você mora na cidade? - Sim, moro. / Não, não moro.
Do you live in the city? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Ela fala português? - Sim, ela fala.
Does she speak Portuguese? Yes, she does.
O que você estuda? - Eu estudo inglês.
What do you study? I study English.
Onde ele trabalha? - Ele trabalha em uma escola.
Where does he work? He works in a school.
Quando eles assistem filmes? - Eles assistem filmes nos fins de semana.
When do they watch movies? They watch movies on weekends.
Por que você quer um carro? - Porque eu preciso para o trabalho.
Why do you want a car? Because I need it for work.
Você tem um cachorro? - Não, tenho um gato.
Do you have a dog? No, I have a cat.
choose: Do you study English? Yes, I ___.

What do you do? I am a student.

Where are you now? I am at home.
Where does she live? She lives in São Paulo.
When is your English class? It's on Monday.
When do you study? I study every night.
Why are you happy? Because it's Friday!
Why do you want to learn English? For my job.
How are you? I'm fine, thanks.
How do you get to school? By bus.

grammar: Choose the question word according to the information wanted: who person, what thing/activity, where place, when time, why reason, how manner/state. After the question word, use be (Who is she? Where are you?) or do/does with other Present Simple verbs (Where does he work? What do you eat?).

Where does he work?

title: I Worked / She Went
vocab: work → worked=trabalhar → trabalhou|watch → watched=assistir → assistiu|play → played=jogar → jogou|cook → cooked=cozinhar → cozinhou|clean → cleaned=limpar → limpou|study → studied=estudar → estudou|go → went=ir → foi|eat → ate=comer → comeu|drink → drank=beber → bebeu|see → saw=ver → viu|have → had=ter → teve|read → read=ler → leu|yesterday=ontem|last night=ontem à noite|last week=semana passada|last weekend=fim de semana passado|this morning=esta manhã|an hour ago=uma hora atrás
context: I watched a movie yesterday.
She worked at the office last week.
They played soccer last weekend.
I went to the park yesterday.
You ate an apple an hour ago.
She drank coffee this morning.
grammar: Past Simple affirmative describes a completed past event. Regular verbs often add -ed (work → worked; watch → watched), while some use an irregular form (go → went, eat → ate). After the subject, use the past form without do/does. Time expressions include yesterday, last night, last week and an hour ago. Read is spelled the same in past but pronounced differently.
grammarExamples: I worked yesterday.
She went to the park yesterday.
He ate lunch an hour ago.
express: Eu assisti um filme ontem.
I watched a movie yesterday.
Ela trabalhou no escritório na semana passada.
She worked at the office last week.
Eles jogaram futebol no fim de semana passado.
They played soccer last weekend.
Ele cozinhou o jantar ontem à noite.
He cooked dinner last night.
Nós limpamos a casa esta manhã.
We cleaned the house this morning.
Eu fui ao parque ontem. Você comeu uma maçã uma hora atrás.
I went to the park yesterday. You ate an apple an hour ago.
Ela bebeu café esta manhã. Ele se divertiu ontem à noite.
She drank coffee this morning. He had fun last night.
choose: You ___ an apple an hour ago.

title: I Didn't Understand / They Didn't Go
vocab: work → worked=trabalhar → trabalhou|cook → cooked=cozinhar → cozinhou|go → went=ir → foi|see → saw=ver → viu|have → had=ter → teve|eat → ate=comer → comeu|movie=filme|soccer=futebol|tv show=programa de TV|dinner=jantar|party=festa|breakfast=café da manhã|didn't=não (did not)
context: I watched a movie, but I didn't watch a TV show.
She went to the park, but she didn't go to school.
They played soccer, but they didn't play basketball.
He cooked dinner, but he didn't cook lunch.
We had a party last weekend, but we didn't have one last night.
I saw my brother, but I didn't see my sister.
chunks: I didn't watch a TV show
grammar: Past Simple negative uses didn't + base verb with every subject: I didn't watch; she didn't go; they didn't play. The verb after didn't stays in base form even when the positive uses an irregular past form: went, but didn't go; saw, but didn't see. Use but to contrast the two facts.
grammarExamples: I watched a movie, but I didn't watch a TV show.
She went to the park, but she didn't go to school.
express: Eu assisti um filme, mas não assisti um programa de TV.
I watched a movie, but I didn't watch a TV show.
Eles jogaram futebol, mas não jogaram basquete.
They played soccer, but they didn't play basketball.
Ele cozinhou o jantar, mas não cozinhou o almoço.
He cooked dinner, but he didn't cook lunch.
Nós fizemos uma festa no fim de semana passado, mas não fizemos uma ontem à noite.
We had a party last weekend, but we didn't have one last night.
Eu vi meu irmão, mas não vi minha irmã.
I saw my brother, but I didn't see my sister.
Você tomou o café da manhã, mas não almoçou porque estava ocupado.
You ate breakfast, but you didn't have lunch because you were busy.
choose: They played soccer, but they ___ play basketball.
gaps: She went to the park, but didn't ___ to school.
We had a party, but we ___ have one last night.
He cooked dinner, but didn't ___ lunch.
I saw my brother, but I didn't ___ my sister.

title: Did You Understand? / Did You Do It?
vocab: work → worked=trabalhar → trabalhou|play → played=jogar → jogou|watch → watched=assistir → assistiu|go → went=ir → foi|see → saw=ver → viu|have → had=ter → teve|eat → ate=comer → comeu|movie=filme|home=casa|school=escola|park=parque|friend=amigo|party=festa|dinner=jantar|last weekend=fim de semana passado|last monday=segunda-feira passada|this morning=esta manhã|did=auxiliar do passado|what=o que|where=onde
context: Did you work yesterday? Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
Did she go to school? Yes, she did.
What did you watch last night? I watched a movie.
Where did they go last weekend? They went to the park.
When did he see his friend? He saw him this morning.
grammar: Past Simple questions use Did + subject + base verb: Did you work? Did she go? Did is already past, so the main verb remains in base form, not went or watched. Short answers: Yes, I did; No, I didn't. Information questions begin with What, Where, When, Who, Why or How followed by did.
grammarExamples: Did you work yesterday? Yes, I did.
Did she go to school? Yes, she did.
Where did they go last weekend? They went to the park.
express: O que você assistiu ontem à noite? - Eu assisti um filme.
What did you watch last night? I watched a movie.
Para onde eles foram no fim de semana passado? - Eles foram ao parque.
Where did they go last weekend? They went to the park.
Quando ele viu o amigo? - Ele o viu esta manhã.
When did he see his friend? He saw him this morning.
Quem você viu na festa? - Eu vi meu irmão.
Who did you see at the party? I saw my brother.
Por que você jantou cedo? - Porque eu estava com fome.
Why did you eat dinner early? Because I was hungry.
Como você voltou para casa? - Eu voltei de ônibus.
How did you get home? I came home by bus.
choose: Did you watch TV? Yes, I ___.
